event.summary: Removing the bare-tmux copy does not bypass remaining archive/static validation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: cb762a313abbe6da03ae0bf041f07486c4ed4df9. TLDR: discovery pass checked a narrower validation-loop concern within the original suspected release-inventory mismatch: deleting the bare-tmux copy must not leave an empty or incompletely inspected binary set. Source analysis found no such bypass. Original hypothetical consequences remain provisioning missing a required executable or publishing an unchecked payload. The earlier c3 evidence retains the exact four-archive inventory match at assets.rs:43-64 and sign-sums.yml:60-64, name-based sums lookup, absence of tmux extra artifacts, and the explicit four-payload contract at SPEC_impl.md:8050-8052,8074-8077. event.summary: Removing the focused shutdown step does not omit surviving shutdown tests
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: considered whether removing the dedicated tmux shutdown gate stopped testing the dangerous output-client teardown that could otherwise crash a server holding sessions. Source checks: the deleted scripts/test-tmux-pinned-shutdown.sh selected ten exact tests. Revision-specific grep finds the three stream unit tests still present in crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/tmux/stream.rs:2632,2724,2845; the seven named e2e tests are absent after the same commit's test migration/removal. The ordinary release step still executes cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude farhelm-desktop against the pinned tmux, so it includes the surviving unit regressions. .config/nextest.toml:1-7 states process-per-test execution, and :36-44 keeps the stream tests in the shared tmux budget; the old separate-step rationale of fresh processes does not add isolation beyond the existing runner. Suggested bucket: other for removing a redundant test invocation; no defect established. Confidence: confirmed source-only refutation of omitted surviving tests. proposed_drop: remaining selected shutdown cases still run in the main release suite, and the retired e2e selectors cannot run after their removal. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: the underlying shutdown hazard could lose running work, but this patch has no established route to that consequence because the surviving shutdown regression coverage remains selected. Caveat: this record does not certify that deleting the e2e tests elsewhere in the commit preserves every legacy-terminal behavior; those test bodies are outside this group's assigned patches.
